title: 医療版マクロ経済スライドは「調整弁」の争いに　主戦場は窓口負担か
extracted_text:
1月の衆院解散で中断していた自民党と日本維新の会の社会保障改革に向けた協議が3月から再び始まった。焦点の一つとなるのが、経済成長率や人口動態に応じて医療費の伸びに上限を設ける「医療版マクロ経済スライド」の導入だ。

両党が2025年10月に交わした連立合意書の社会保障分野は13項目ある。冒頭に掲げたのが「インフレ下での医療給付費のあり方と、現役世代の保険料負担抑制との整合性を図るための制度的対応」だ。

議論再開初日の3月19日はこの項目を話し合い、維新は医療費の伸びを名目GDP（国内総生産）に連動させる仕組みを提起した。

年金では04年の制度改正で、支給額を経済状況に応じて自動的に抑えるマクロ経済スライドが導入された。医療にも同じような総額管理を適用しようとする議論は、四半世紀前から繰り返されてきた。

代表例は小泉純一郎政権下の01年。厚生労働省は70歳以上を対象に当時の老人医療費制度へ伸び率の抑制目標を導入する案を打ち出した。財務省は医療費全体を対象とし、目標超過分は診療報酬引き下げで調整する対案を唱えた。ともに実現に至らなかった。

年金や介護も含めた社会保障費は野放しに膨らんできたわけではない。例えば16年度予算以降は、毎年の国費について高齢化の伸びの範囲に抑える歳出の目安が導入された。

財務省の幹部は「デフレ時代だった当時は経済・物価が動かない分、高齢化の範囲までは面倒を見ようという考えだった。インフレで人件費や物件費があがる時代の医療費の伸びを抑えようとするならマクロ経済スライド的な発想が必要になる」と話す。

布石は打たれている。片山さつき財務相と上野賢一郎厚生労働相は25年12月、閣僚折衝の合意文書に「27年度の社会保障負担率が25年度と比較して上昇しないよう取り組む」との一文を盛り込んだ。年金や介護も含めた負担率は国民所得比で25年度に17.8%を見込む。

医療は年金とは異なる。新型コロナウイルスのようなパンデミック（世界的な大流行）や高額な新薬の登場といったイノベーションを伴い、予測が難しい。厚労省幹部は医療費の伸びに枠をはめれば「産業としての医療を抑え込みかねない」と危惧する。

いまも高齢化の伸びをはみ出す分は制度改革でカットしている。その上で保険料の負担率を一定にコントロールするなら、伸び続ける医療費の「調整弁」は患者が受診時に払う窓口負担か、税財源を増やすしかない。

維新は現役世代の保険料負担抑制を掲げ、消費税については高市早苗首相と歩調を合わせ2年間に限り食料品の税率をゼロとする立場を取る。公費と保険料で賄う給付費を抑え込むのなら、窓口負担の引き上げが選択肢にならざるを得ない。

赤字国債の発行拡大に頼る余裕が財政にない以上、痛みの再分配が改革の成否を決める。両党は5月末までに骨子をつくり、年度内に具体的な制度設計に入る。

translated_text: The negotiations between the LDP and Nippon Ishin no Kai on social security reform, which were interrupted when the Lower House was dissolved in January, resumed in March. One key focus is the introduction of a 'medical version macroeconomic slide' that would cap the growth of medical expenses based on economic growth rates and demographic trends. The two parties' October 2025 coalition agreement contains 13 items in the social security sector. The first item states 'institutional responses to ensure consistency between medical benefit costs under inflation and restraining premium burdens on the working generation.' On March 19th, the first day talks resumed, Ishin proposed a mechanism linking medical expense growth to nominal GDP. In pensions, a macroeconomic slide that automatically restrains benefit amounts based on economic conditions was introduced in the 2004 system reforms. Discussions on applying similar total expenditure management to medical care have been recurring for a quarter-century. The most representative example was during the Koizumi Junichiro administration in 2001. The Ministry of Health proposed a plan to introduce growth rate restraint targets for the then-elderly medical expense system targeting those aged 70 and older. The Ministry of Finance proposed an alternative targeting all medical expenses, with excess amounts adjusted through medical fee reductions. Neither was realized. Social security costs including pensions and care have not grown unchecked. For example, since the FY2016 budget, annual national expenditure guidelines have been introduced to contain spending within the range of aging-related growth. A senior Finance Ministry official says, 'During the deflation era, since the economy and prices weren't moving, the thinking was to provide care up to the extent of aging-related growth. If you try to restrain medical expense growth in an era when labor and material costs are rising due to inflation, you need a macroeconomic-slide-type approach.' The groundwork has been laid. Finance Minister Katayama Yoshimi and Health Minister Ueno Kenichiro included in December 2025 a cabinet-level agreement stating they 'will work to ensure the social security burden rate does not increase compared to FY2025.' The burden rate including pensions and care is expected to be 17.8% of national income in FY2025. Medical care is different from pensions. It's difficult to predict due to pandemics like COVID-19 and innovative new expensive drugs. Health Ministry officials worry that setting limits on medical expense growth could 'end up suppressing medical care as an industry.' Even now, portions exceeding aging-related growth are cut through system reforms. On top of that, to keep premium burden rates constant, the 'adjustment valve' for ever-increasing medical expenses can only be out-of-pocket costs when patients visit medical offices, or increasing tax revenues. Ishin advocates restraining premium burdens on the working generation, and regarding the consumption tax, aligns with Prime Minister Abe Takashi in taking the position of limiting the food product tax rate to zero for two years only. If they want to restrain benefit costs covered by public funds and premiums, raising out-of-pocket costs becomes an unavoidable option. With no fiscal leeway to rely on expanding deficit bond issuance, pain redistribution will determine reform success or failure. The two parties will create a framework by the end of May and begin specific system design within the fiscal year.
title_en: Medical Macroeconomic Slide: Battle Over 'Adjustment Valve' - Main Battlefront May Be Copayments
